function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is an official authorization or instruction that gives a person or organization the authority to act on behalf of another party. In many contexts—especially in finance, law, and business—a mandate defines the scope, limits, and responsibilities of the authorized entity. Here are a few common uses:

| Context | What the mandate means |
|---------|------------------------|
| **Banking / Finance** | A mandate is a formal instruction (often in the form of a signed document) that allows a bank or financial institution to execute transactions on behalf of a client. For example, a standing order or a direct debit mandate lets the bank transfer money automatically. |
| **Legal / Corporate** | A mandate can be a directive from a board or shareholders that empowers a manager or a committee to make decisions within specified limits. |
| **Government / Public Sector** | A mandate is a directive from a higher authority (e.g., a minister or parliament) that authorizes a department or agency to carry out certain policies or actions. |
| **Partnerships / Partnerships** | In a partnership, a mandate may refer to the authority granted to a partner to act on behalf of the partnership in dealings with third parties. |

In short, a mandate is a formal, often written, authorization that sets out what an agent or representative is allowed to do for the principal.
